title: Quantum critical superconductivity in a dense fermi dilute bose mixture close to mechanical instability
abstract: We couple a metal to an uncondensed bose gas with repulsive bose-fermi interactions in two dimensions. Within the random phase approximation, we show that the density fluctuations of the bosons, which mediate the effective fermion-fermion attraction, become long ranged on appropriate tuning of interactions. This leads to parametrically enhanced superconducting temperatures $T_c \propto g$ as opposed to $T_c \propto \exp(-1/g)$ for the BCS case. The dilute bose gas density acts as the primary bottleneck to the enhancement. We discuss the conceptual difficulties of implementing this idea in electron-exciton mixtures.
summary: This theoretical work explores enhancing superconductivity in a Fermi-Bose mixture by coupling electrons to a dilute Bose gas. By analyzing density fluctuations using RPA, the authors demonstrate that the resulting attraction can lead to an algebraic enhancement of $T_c$ rather than the typical exponential BCS dependence. This suggests a powerful mechanism for designing novel superconducting materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates mechanisms to enhance superconducting transition temperatures ($T_c$) by coupling fermions (electrons) to a bosonic gas (e.g., excitons or dilute bosons).
main_result: The coupling can lead to an effective attraction that results in an algebraic dependence for $T_c$ ($T_c \propto g$), significantly surpassing the exponential dependence found in standard BCS theory.
method: The analysis employs the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) and utilizes renormalization group (RG) techniques to analyze the flow of pairing channels and calculate the fermion self-energy.
model_or_system: The model is a two-dimensional system consisting of a metal (fermions) coupled to an uncondensed Bose gas with repulsive Bose-Fermi interactions. The analysis covers both deeply degenerate and non-degenerate temperature regimes.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), fermion self-energy ($\Sigma(i\omega)$), and the effective pairing strength ($g$).
important_parameters: Boson density (acts as a bottleneck), interaction coupling constant ($\lambda$), and the ratio of energy scales ($\Lambda$ vs $\Lambda'$).
main_assumptions: The use of RPA, the validity of the T-matrix approximation for the boson self-energy, and the assumption that long-range density fluctuations drive the pairing enhancement.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the model system: dense electrons interacting with dilute excitons.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general model Hamiltonian and the standard BCS comparison, moves through detailed calculations of the boson polarization function ($\Pi_b$) in different temperature regimes, and culminates in deriving the enhanced $T_c$ via the self-energy calculation.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete theoretical pathway to engineer high-$T_c$ superconductors by leveraging quantum critical fluctuations from bosonic baths, which is highly relevant to modern condensed matter research.
